chapters.title: The Egg in the Mango Tree
lines: A storm shakes Aata-gram. An egg rolls out of the old mango tree.
Chilaka the parrot hatches and blinks at you. Its first word is 'print'.
Grandmother Ammamma smiles: 'A village grows one small spell at a time.'

chapters.title: The Broken Gate
lines: The village gate will not open. A sign says: age 18 or more.
Chilaka squawks that the sign says 'age = 18', not 'age >= 18'.
You fix the condition and the gate swings wide. Doors are logic.

chapters.title: The Water Wheel
lines: The wheel stopped turning and the fields are dry.
The old keeper counted rounds by hand and lost track.
Loops keep it moving. You write one and water runs again.

chapters.title: The Letter Market
lines: Traders shout names in a hundred ways: RAVI, ravi, Ravi.
Chilaka learns that text can be cleaned, cut and joined.
By evening every stall sign is neat and the market sings.

chapters.title: The Granary Lists
lines: The granary overflows with sacks nobody has counted.
Lists keep order, dictionaries keep labels, sets keep only one of each.
You sort the sacks. Ammamma nods: 'Now we know what we have.'

chapters.title: The Machine Shed
lines: Ammamma's tools repeat the same job all day.
You teach a machine to do a job once and call it any time.
The shed hums. Functions are tools that remember how.

chapters.title: The Mistake Pond
lines: Things fall into the pond: bad numbers, missing files, wrong guesses.
Chilaka does not panic. It catches each one and carries on.
You learn that errors are messages, not enemies.

chapters.title: The Helper Library
lines: A traveling librarian arrives with shelves of ready-made tools.
'Why build a wheel twice?' she asks, and lends you import.
You also learn to read a traceback like a map of where it hurt.

chapters.title: The Workshop of Things
lines: Villagers want a Dog that barks and a Wallet that remembers.
Classes let you make many things from one plan.
Chilaka chirps: each thing has its own memory, called self.

chapters.title: The Tidy House
lines: Your code works, but it looks like a nest after a storm.
Names, small functions and honest comments make it kind to the next reader.
Ammamma says: 'Write for the person who reads it next. That is often you.'

chapters.title: The Puzzle Fair
lines: Travelers bring riddles: find the pair, guess the number, escape the maze.
You learn that speed comes from clever steps, not just fast hands.
Chilaka wins a ribbon for the neatest trick.

chapters.title: The Bigger World
lines: A road leaves the village toward real servers, real logs and real APIs.
Chilaka sits on your shoulder, grown and bright.
'Go,' says Ammamma. 'The village will be here. Aata-gram lives in what you build.'
